shared_grammar.rule: NP_a BINARY_RELATION NP_b yields the linguistic predication R(a,b), with two actually written role NPs.

INTRODUCE RECORD_NP [NP_a BINARY_RELATION NP_b] STORE supplies account s whose result is r=R(a,b), and whose reusable pattern is F=lambda x.R(a,x). The second role is the open parameter. No diagram or invented helper supplies a/b.

REUSE NP_c has the same unary explicit valency at both sites and in both readings. It contributes local TOPIC(c); TOKEN returns the earlier result r unchanged, while PATTERN returns F(c). TOPIC is a paid aboutness contribution of the written operand, not an English filler or a manuscript fact.
[REUSE NP_c] INSPECT gives INSPECT(returned correspondence). This is an actual written predicate at .35G009, not a saved diagnostic object.

DEPENDENT_ITEM_REFERENCE projects the second argument of the latest reused correspondence; it is a written NP at .36G009. The chosen antecedent, role projection and last-reuse rule are all C0 assumptions.

NP USE gives USE(NP) at .36G009–G010. Ordinary infix relation, prefix reuse and postfix transitive consumers are explicit grammar assumptions; no universal prefix grammar or old renderer values are imported.

Unknown spans remain syntactically opaque. The displayed final dependency is conditional on those spans not replacing s, negating a consumer, changing reuse scope, or changing the projected role. This is an unresolved requirement, not an implemented rule assigning UNKNOWN groups no-op meanings.
